title: Retain desktop shell during audit child exit
summary: Prevents a direct Tauri exit request from closing the desktop shell when the backend refuses or cannot confirm a safe shutdown during active work such as an audit.
reason: An audit launch exited abnormally and the desktop application closed even though Windows remained healthy. The direct app-exit path requested safe backend shutdown but did not prevent the native exit when shutdown was blocked or unavailable.
behavior_before: RunEvent::ExitRequested always allowed the native Tauri process to exit after requesting safe backend shutdown, even when the backend reported active work or the shutdown request failed.
behavior_after: RunEvent::ExitRequested prevents native exit unless backend-owned safe shutdown is acknowledged; blocked or failed shutdown keeps the desktop shell open while active work remains protected.
tests_added: test_tauri_shell_uses_safe_only_shutdown_for_unconfirmed_exit_paths asserts that direct exit requests prevent native shell shutdown when backend shutdown is blocked or fails.
manual_validation: Observed the audit start, its abnormal child-process disappearance, and desktop-backend closure without a corresponding Windows reboot, bugcheck, or application-fault event.
rollback_plan: Revert the RunEvent::ExitRequested branch in apps/desktop/tauri/src-tauri/src/lib.rs and restore the prior static lifecycle assertion if the shell must permit direct exit despite an unsafe backend state.
notes:
Track desktop audit-close investigation and lifecycle hardening.
Prevent direct Tauri exit requests from closing the shell when safe backend shutdown is blocked or unavailable.
Cover direct-exit prevention when backend shutdown is unsafe.
Refresh lifecycle shell summary after direct-exit guard change.
Refresh regression-test summary after shell exit coverage update.
